question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Lefteris Nikolaou-Alavanos (NI), Kostas Papadakis (NI) Subject:

Following the criminal attack by the US and Israel on Iran and the dangerous plans to transform Gaza into an American protectorate, Israel is now also promoting the partition of Lebanon. Under the pretext of eradicating Hezbollah, it has created a so-called ‘peace plan’, in which it provides for the permanent presence of Israeli troops and the creation of a buffer zone. This is reflected in the map published by the Israeli army with the occupied territories in southern Lebanon, which also extends to a corresponding maritime zone – a move that is by no means accidental, since the Israeli-Lebanese maritime border is crucial for the establishment of an EEZ in the Eastern Mediterranean, an area with significant energy reserves. In fact, the Commission defends its involvement in the creation of the spurious ‘Peace Council’, under the pretext that the US, Israel and their allies will supposedly guarantee peace! The Vice-President / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy is asked: 1.

What view does she take of the State of Israel’s unacceptable invasion of Lebanon and of Israel’s plans to split Lebanon into three by imposing an Israeli military occupation zone on the country and creating ‘buffer zones’ to the detriment of Lebanon’s territorial integrity?

What view does she take of the call for an immediate halt to the EU-Israel Association Agreement and to all forms of EU cooperation with Israel, as the peoples are urgently demanding through their struggle?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.6.2026) The EU has continuously called upon Israel to respect Lebanon’s sovereignty and territorial integrity1. The proposal to establish a buffer zone in southern Lebanon raises serious legal, political and humanitarian concerns. It also risks fuelling more sectarian tensions and displacements and to exacerbate the current crisis in Lebanon. The EU also strongly condemns Hezbollah’s attacks against Israel. Hezbollah poses an existential threat to Lebanon and its disarmament remains a priority. The EU urges Israel to stop military operations in the country which are having a dramatic humanitarian and socioeconomic impact. The EU calls on all parties to respect the recently agreed temporary ceasefire, fully supports the continuation of bilateral dialogue between Israel and Lebanon and encourages negotiations as a path toward lasting stability and de-escalation in line with UN Security Council Resolution 1701. In 2025, in light of the catastrophic situation in Gaza, the High Representative/Vice-President conducted, with the support of a majority of Member States, a review of Israel’s compliance with its obligations under Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement2. The conclusion of the review was that there are indications that Israel would be in breach of its obligations. Following the review, the Commission’s President announced a set of proposed measures, including a reinforced package of sanctions and the suspension of certain trade-related provisions of the EU-Israel Association Agreement. The Commission has also put on hold its bilateral support to Israel, with the exception of support to civil society and Yad Vashem. Discussions continue in the Council on other measures which require approval of Member States.
